tasks.short: Observe students at work in the workshop, read written assignments against the rubric, write feedback, publish it to students, and discuss progress and suggestions one to one.

steps.what: Vocational teacher observes students' practical work to determine progress
Vocational teacher reads and evaluates written assignments against the rubric
Vocational teacher writes feedback and suggestions for improvement on each assignment

loop.input: The teacher's notes per rubric item and the student's submitted work.
loop.output: Draft feedback per rubric item in plain language.
loop.check: Each feedback item must quote a passage from the student's work, or it is dropped; the teacher edits and approves all feedback; the model sets no grade.
loop.stop: Stops when the teacher approves, or when a rubric item has no quoted passage and the teacher writes that item.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback must refer to each student's own work; a fixed comment bank reads as generic.

steps.what: Vocational teacher publishes the feedback to students in the learning environment
Vocational teacher discusses progress and suggestions with each student

tasks.design: Before the teacher reads, code in the learning environment ({LMS}) checks length, required sections and source format. A bounded step drafts feedback per rubric item from the teacher's notes, quoting the student's own text; the teacher edits it, and once approved it is published to the student. Grades stay with the teacher as examiner. Observing practical work and talking with students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback on every assignment was written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments can draft rubric feedback from instructor notes.
tasks.still_hard: Students may read drafted feedback as less personal.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in the workshop that a student's confidence, not skill, holds them back.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits feedback drafts instead of writing each from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether revisions improve after drafted feedback.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
In a randomised trial with 354 students and 1,366 essays, assistants agreed with 88% of AI rubric suggestions and student revisions were significantly better.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3, so the model may only draft feedback, never grade.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's work to the progress discussion; grading is outside.
Input contract: rubrics set by the teaching team; notes by the teacher; fallback is writing feedback by hand.
Observing and discussing do not change.
Students read feedback in the learning environment as they do today.
unknowns: Written assignments per student per term.
research_questions: How much of the drafted feedback does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Vocational teacher edits and approves drafted feedback.

incremental.description: Vocational teacher keeps rubric notes in the form the drafting step needs.

approvals.approved_version: The feedback as edited and approved by the teacher in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly practical work with little written feedback; high: many written assignments per term.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare slides and visual aids, present lectures, conduct class discussions, publish slides to students, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Vocational teacher prepares slides, graphs, charts and videos for the lesson
Vocational teacher presents lectures using visual aids
Vocational teacher conducts discussions to increase students' knowledge and competence
Vocational teacher uploads the slides for students
Vocational teacher answers students' follow-up questions by e-mail

tasks.design: The teaching team keeps one shared library of slide decks and visual aids per learning outcome in the document space ({DOCS}), so each teacher adapts an existing deck instead of building one. Once the teacher has finished the deck, it is published to the class in the learning environment ({LMS}) on a set time. Presenting and leading discussions stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each teacher built and kept their own slides.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document spaces and learning environments hold versioned course materials.
tasks.still_hard: Teachers like their own way of telling a topic.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a student's story from their internship into the lesson's example.

reach.learn: Whether shared decks cut preparation time.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces and learning environments can hold versioned course materials per learning outcome.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson plan to questions answered; curriculum design is outside.
Input contract: learning outcomes from the curriculum; decks shared by the teaching team; fallback is each teacher's own slides.
Presenting and discussing do not change.

incremental.description: Vocational teacher updates shared decks after teaching.

approvals.approved_version: The slide deck as finished by the teacher in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one teacher per course; high: several teachers teaching the same course.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check which students passed the tool safety instruction, demonstrate safe use, supervise and monitor students using tools and equipment, and log tool faults and damage.

steps.what: Vocational teacher checks the paper list of students who passed the tool safety instruction
Vocational teacher demonstrates safe use of tools and equipment
Vocational teacher supervises and monitors students' use of tools and equipment
Vocational teacher logs tool faults and damage on a paper form

tasks.design: Safety instruction results are recorded in the learning environment ({LMS}) and shown per student and machine on the teacher's tablet, so the teacher does not search a paper list. Each machine carries a QR code that opens a fault form for the workshop technician. Demonstrating and supervising stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety clearance was on paper lists and faults on paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments record instruction results; QR codes open fault forms.
tasks.still_hard: A student who passed the instruction can still use a tool unsafely.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping in the moment a student's hand gets too close to a blade.

evidence.claim: Learning environments can record safety instruction results per student; QR codes can open fault forms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the class list to the fault report; tool repair is outside.
Input contract: instruction results recorded by the teacher who gave it; fallback is the paper list.
Demonstrating and supervising do not change.

incremental.description: Vocational teacher records new instruction results.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one small workshop with few machines; high: large workshops with many machines and students.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile the test from the item bank, administer written tests, conduct oral and performance tests, mark written work, decide results, enter grades, and review item analysis for training effectiveness.

steps.what: Vocational teacher compiles the test from earlier items or writes new ones
Vocational teacher administers written tests on paper
Vocational teacher conducts oral and performance tests with the rubric
Vocational teacher marks written tests
Vocational teacher decides the results as examiner
Vocational teacher types the grades into the student administration system
Vocational teacher reviews item scores to evaluate training effectiveness

tasks.design: Tests are compiled from an item bank in the test system ({LMS}) with each item's earlier statistics. Written tests are taken on school laptops; closed questions are marked by code and open answers are marked by the teacher in the same screen. The test system shows item analysis per question. Once the teacher has decided the results as examiner, the grades pass to the student administration system ({OTHER}) without retyping. Oral and performance tests stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were on paper, marked by hand and grades typed into two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Test systems mark closed questions, show item statistics and pass grades to student administration.
tasks.still_hard: Performance tests in the workshop do not fit a test system.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a student really can do the job, not just pass the test.

ambition.what: Review item analysis after every test instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The teacher marks open answers and decides; counting and retyping go.

evidence.claim: At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, a double entry.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results, and only the board sanctions fraud.

assumptions: Boundary: from learning outcomes to registered grades and item analysis; resits are outside.
Input contract: items written by the teaching team; grades passed to student administration by a link; fallback is paper tests and typing.
Oral and performance tests and deciding results do not change.
Students take digital tests in about the same time as paper ones.
research_questions: Do weak items get replaced sooner?

incremental.description: Vocational teacher tags items in the item bank by learning outcome.

approvals.approved_version: The results as decided by the teacher as examiner in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly performance tests; high: mostly written tests with closed questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The vocational teacher keeps teaching, observing, supervising and deciding results; writing feedback from scratch, building slides alone, paper lists and typing grades shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time in the workshop with students.
